Key Activities: Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Provides advice to users on the methods and procedures related to statistical operations services.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on various teams and working groups.
Leads the activities of work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations.

1. Decision making: Develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Outlines proposals for changes and improvements to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data, and the implementation and use of new hardware and software options to support survey development and assessment.

Determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity, reviews operational processes, and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications.
Prepares and implements policies and guidelines to maintain the integrity, security and 'back-up' systems and processes.
Reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations. Documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement statistical production activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information; responds orally or in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to establish and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities, to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada.
Writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.
Participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the statistical and economic concepts and principles used in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data in order to recommend and implement improvements to survey collection, coding and processing activities.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to oversee the design, testing, operation and maintenance of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of project and time management methods, practices and techniques to develop work plans, estimate resource requirements and to monitor and report on work progress.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to identify potential sources of information for operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.
Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to understand and explain the need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on survey concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Researches options and requirements for the operation of divisional statistical systems and processes in order to assist in the establishment of divisional and program objectives and priorities.

Reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data. This requires interpreting or adapting practices.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.
